Step 1: Extract relevant information.
The question asks what percentage of packed shoes I wore on my last trip. The memory items include packing conversations (items 1 and 2), covering tops, bottoms, undergarments, socks, and toiletries. Item 1 mentions black pants, shorts, a white t-shirt, a gray sweater, and a blouse, but no shoes. Item 2 covers a 5-day city trip with tops, undergarments, and socks, again with no shoes. Other items cover fitness apps, business class, environmental tips, skiing, San Francisco walks, exercise, and collectibles. None mention how many pairs of shoes were packed or worn.

Step 2: Reason.
Answering would require two numbers: the pairs of shoes packed and the pairs actually worn. Neither appears anywhere in the memory. The packing discussions are also about planned trips, not a completed trip with a record of what was worn. So no percentage can be computed.

Answer: I can't determine this from our past conversations. You haven't told me how many pairs of shoes you packed or how many you wore on your last trip. If you give me those two numbers, I can calculate the percentage (worn ÷ packed × 100).
